title: Rosh Hashanah: hearing the shofar
hook: the mitzvah is to hear it, fully present
tomorrow: seek God "while He may be found." when can't you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the simanim: a pomegranate, a date, a fish head, each eaten with a wish for the year. A wish on a plate. Today the holiday's other sense: not taste, but sound.
screen: `A WISH ON A PLATE.` → `NOT TASTE, BUT SOUND.`

segments.voice: Earbuds in, a podcast at double speed, a voice memo skipped to the end. Plenty of sound gets half-heard. Now a scene the Mishnah sets on Rosh Hashanah morning. A man walks past a synagogue. Through the open window comes a long, raw note from a ram's horn, the shofar. Another man walks past the same window and hears the same note. Both keep walking. And the Mishnah says one of them has kept the day's commandment, and the other hasn't. Same street, same sound. What's the difference?
screen: `A PODCAST AT DOUBLE SPEED.` → `TWO MEN PASS THE SAME WINDOW.` → `ONE HAS KEPT IT. ONE HASN'T.`

segments.voice: The Mishnah's answer: the one who directed his heart. Same note, but one man was listening and the other only heard. That's the shofar on Rosh Hashanah. The Torah calls the day "a memorial proclaimed with the blast of horns," and the blessing said before the blowing isn't about blowing at all. It thanks God for the commandment to hear the sound of the shofar. One person does the work; everyone else's job is to hear. So the room goes still. There are three sounds. Tekiah: one long, unbroken note. Shevarim: broken notes, like sobbing. Teruah: a rattle of short blasts, like an alarm. Tradition counts a hundred notes across the morning, and the custom is to hear them all, no talking in between. Why a horn and not words? Maimonides says the blowing is simply a decree of scripture, and still he hears a hint in it: wake up, sleepers, from your sleep; search your deeds and come back. A horn can't be skimmed. And some congregations carry a shofar to people who can't come, the sick and the homebound, so the sound reaches them too.
screen: `THE ONE WHO DIRECTED HIS HEART.` · `THE BLESSING: TO HEAR.` · `TEKIAH, SHEVARIM, TERUAH.` · `WAKE UP, SLEEPERS.` · then, large: `HEAR EVERY NOTE.`

segments.voice: Set your phone face down. For the sit, choose one sound that's already there: a fan, traffic, a bird, your own breath. Hear it all the way through, each time it comes, the way a room waits for the next note. When your mind wanders off, that's the man who kept walking; come back to the window.
screen: `PHONE FACE DOWN.` · `ONE SOUND, ALL THE WAY THROUGH.` · `BACK TO THE WINDOW.`

segments.voice: Rosh Hashanah: head of the year. The Jewish new year, when the shofar sounds, and the commandment is to hear it.
Your line: hear every note. The blower does the work; the listening is yours. Shanah tovah.

screen: `DAY 1681 COUNTS.` → `THE YEAR, LIVED · 4 OF 30.` → `TOMORROW: "WHILE HE MAY BE FOUND." WHEN CAN'T YOU?`

howItsDone: On Rosh Hashanah the shofar is blown in synagogue during the morning service, and the congregation stands quietly to hear each sound; some communities also bring the shofar to people who are homebound or in the hospital.

chat.meaning: The blessing is to hear the shofar, and the Mishnah counts only the listener whose heart was in it. Every note gets heard.

shofar.meaning: a ram's horn, sounded on Rosh Hashanah
